app.name: Atlassian (Jira, Confluence)
app.oneLiner: Jira and Confluence Cloud use one OAuth 2.0 model, called 3LO, registered in the Atlassian Developer Console. Private by default, shareable by a toggle, reviewed only for the Marketplace.

oauth.notes: Atlassian calls collecting end-user API tokens, or asking each customer to create their own 3LO app, non-compliant with its security requirements. Build one distributable 3LO app.

summary.difficultyReason: Creating and sharing the app takes under an hour and needs no review. The catch: until Atlassian has reviewed the app (a Marketplace process), users see a warning that it has not been reviewed.

timeToProduction.note: Sharing with a privacy policy URL is enough for any user to install, with an 'unreviewed' warning. Removing the warning means a Marketplace listing; its review time is not documented here.

summary.cost: Free to create and share. Marketplace listing has its own program requirements.

blockers.text: Installers of an app Atlassian has not reviewed are warned that it has not been reviewed. Only a Marketplace review removes this.

summary.tldr: Register an OAuth 2.0 (3LO) integration in the Developer Console, add one callback URL, pick scopes, then flip Distribution to Sharing with a vendor name and privacy policy URL. Any Atlassian user can then install it, with an 'unreviewed app' warning until you go through Marketplace review.

prerequisites.text: An Atlassian account. No separate developer-program enrolment is needed for a 3LO integration.
A public privacy policy URL. Required the moment you enable sharing.
A Jira or Confluence Cloud site to test against (free plans work).

evidence.note: standard practice; not stated as a requirement in the console docs

dev.title: Open the Developer Console
dev.detail: From any developer.atlassian.com page, profile icon, then Developer console. Your 3LO apps are listed with a 3LO lozenge.

dev.title: Create an OAuth 2.0 integration
dev.detail: Create, then OAuth 2.0 integration. Enter the app name and accept the developer terms. The app is private by default: only you can install it.

dev.title: Add the 3LO callback URL
dev.detail: Authorization, then next to OAuth 2.0 (3LO) click Add and enter your callback URL. One callback URL per app; use separate apps for local and production environments.

dev.title: Add the Jira (or Confluence) API and pick scopes
dev.detail: Permissions, add the Jira API, Edit Scopes, select the minimum. Add the API before editing scopes, and set Authorization first or scope edits may not stick. Include offline_access in your authorize request if you need refresh tokens.
dev.consoleLocation: Permissions > Jira API > Add > Edit Scopes

values.value: add offline_access to the authorize URL scope list

dev.title: Copy client ID and secret
dev.detail: Settings in the left menu shows both. Put them into your integration or your Composio custom auth config.

dev.title: Authorize against your own site
dev.detail: Run the authorization URL from the Authorization page. The user picks which site to grant at consent; tokens are site-scoped, so you call the API via api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/{cloudid}/… after looking up accessible resources.

production.title: Enable sharing
production.detail: Distribution, Edit, choose Sharing. You must enter at least a vendor name and a privacy policy URL, and select a personal data declaration. Users can now install from the authorization link.

values.value: choose the option that matches whether you store Atlassian personal data

production.title: Decide whether to pursue a Marketplace listing
production.detail: Shared-but-unreviewed apps show a 'not yet reviewed by Atlassian' warning at install. A Marketplace listing adds security requirements and a review. For an internal tool or a private beta, sharing is enough.
production.effort: days to weeks if you list

evidence.note: listing requirements and timing are outside the pages checked for this guide

requirements.notes: Only to remove the unreviewed warning and be discoverable.

gotchas.title: Site-scoped tokens
gotchas.detail: Access tokens apply to the site the user selected at consent. Call GET https://api.atlassian.com/oauth/token/accessible-resources to find cloud IDs, then route requests through api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/{cloudid}.

gotchas.title: Do not collect API tokens from end users
gotchas.detail: Atlassian names collecting customer API tokens, or instructing each customer to create their own 3LO app, as non-compliant with its security requirements and acceptable use policy.

gotchas.title: Order of operations in the console
gotchas.detail: Set Authorization (callback URL) before editing scopes, and add the API before Edit Scopes appears; integrators report scope edits failing otherwise.

gotchas.title: You cannot delete an installed app
gotchas.detail: Uninstall it from every site before deleting the app in Settings.

whenStuck.action: Use an absolute https URL with no wildcard; for local development use a tunnel URL rather than http://localhost.

whenStuck.situation: Users ask why they see a warning at install
whenStuck.action: Explain the app is shared but not Marketplace-reviewed; if the warning blocks adoption, start the Marketplace listing process.

corrected: Initial draft assumed sharing needed only a toggle; StackOne and Nango walkthroughs show the console requires vendor name, privacy policy URL and a personal data declaration, so those were added as hard requirements.
unverifiable: Whether Atlassian serves OAuth discovery metadata (probe not run; auth.atlassian.com is the authorization server, not www.atlassian.com)
verification.notes: The official console page confirms private-by-default, sharing, and the unreviewed warning. Field names come from three independent integrator walkthroughs that agree with each other.

openQuestions: Marketplace listing review time and whether a security self-assessment is required for 3LO apps (as opposed to Forge/Connect) was not checked.
Rotating refresh token behaviour: Atlassian has changed this before; confirm current expiry in the 3LO docs before relying on long-lived refresh tokens.
